raw_response:
I’ve been farming these 6 mu for 25 years. My father farmed them before me. I never went to school, but I know this land — I know which corner stays wet and which dries out first when the sun hits.

This year it’s me, my wife, and my old mother at home. My two sons work in the city making furniture. They send money back, but I don’t like using it for the farm — they have their own children to feed. So I’m working with what I have in my pocket. Cash is tight, and every yuan matters.

**Winter wheat:** I plant all 6 mu. I saved my own seed from last year — it’s a local red wheat that’s been in the village for years. No need to buy seed, that saves me money. I plant around October 10th, same as always. Before planting, I spread about half a bag of compound fertilizer per mu — that’s 50 jin. I till it in with the tractor.

In March, when the wheat wakes up (返青), I topdress about 30 jin of urea per mu. If the wheat looks yellow at jointing (拔节), maybe I’ll throw another 15 jin, but probably not — urea went up in price and I’d rather have cash in hand for emergencies. I’ll irrigate three times: once after the topdress, once at jointing, and once when the grain is filling. Each time costs me electricity for the pump, so I watch the sky. If it rains good, maybe I skip one, but last year was dry so I’ll likely do all three.

For weeds, I spray herbicide once in spring. If I see aphids, I’ll spray insecticide, but I wait and watch first. Insecticide is expensive.

**Summer maize:** As soon as the wheat comes off in early June — around June 8th or so — I have to get the maize in quick. The window is maybe 4-5 days. I hire the neighbor’s tractor for one light pass, then plant. No time for deep tillage. I buy hybrid maize seed every year — about 3 jin per mu, costs me around 45 yuan per mu. Everyone knows you can’t save maize seed.

At planting, I put down the same amount of compound fertilizer as wheat — half a bag per mu. Then at big trumpet (大喇叭口), I side-dress about 40 jin of urea per mu. That’s when the maize is hungriest. I’ll irrigate twice: once at jointing and once at filling. If the summer rains are good, maybe once is enough, but I don’t trust the sky anymore.

I spray herbicide on the maize about 10 days after it comes up. Insecticide only if I see worms.

**Labor:** It’s mostly me and my wife. My mother can watch the pump and cook for us. For wheat harvest, I hire the combine — 50 yuan per mu — and hire one person to help bag and load for a couple days. For maize, if the machine can get in, I hire it. If not, it’s hand-picking, and I’ll hire a few people from the village.

**Money:** I expect about 400 kg per mu of wheat and maybe 450 kg per mu of maize if the weather is fair. Last year I got a bit less because it was dry. I’m not getting younger, and the soil is getting tired, but I can’t afford to let it rest. Every mu has to work.
